title: Learning: One Letter Off
text: A developer adds an HTTP library. The build system resolves the name, and the registry decides where that name comes from.
held: The name was read, and it resolved from where it was supposed to.

cards.label: Resolve it and write the lockfile
Reject the change
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: package name
fields.check: Read the package name letter by letter

intrusion.detail: reqeusts: two letters swapped. Not the library you think it is.
intrusion.why: A typo in a dependency name installs whatever someone registered under the typo. That is a stranger's code in your build.
intrusion.reveal: The dependency was spelled reqeusts, a look-alike of the real library.

temptations.label: Check that the package is popular: plenty of downloads and stars
temptations.why: Popularity can be bought or inflated, and a look-alike name borrows the real package's reputation. Identity is the exact name and publisher, not a count.

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: resolves from
fields.check: Check which index this name resolves from
fields.ok: The private index, where the company publishes it.

intrusion.value: the public index, under the same name
intrusion.detail: The public index has a package with this internal name, at a higher version.
intrusion.why: An internal name answered by the public index is dependency confusion: whoever registered it there gets their code into your build.
intrusion.reveal: The internal package name billing-utils was being answered by the public index.

teaches: A dependency name is an instruction to run someone's code. Read it.
Internal names must resolve from internal sources only; otherwise a public package of the same name wins.
Tools that guess the name you meant are guessing on an attacker's behalf.
